schedule.rationale: At Risk because the 20 January sign-off needs documentation that does not exist in usable form, and the replacement cannot start before late February (signals S1, S5, S6). The March 2027 scale-up date is not realistic on the current plan.

scope.rationale: Problematic because the pilot is stable at 15% of claims, but the scope to all claims depends on sign-off and a retraining process that currently only two leavers understand (S3, S7). No cost estimate for the scale-up is in the scenario.

quality.rationale: Problematic because triage accuracy is 87%, above the 85% target, and handling time is down 22%. However, accuracy has fallen from 89% over two months since the claim form change, and the cause is not yet confirmed (S4).

risk_control.rationale: At Risk because retraining scripts sit in a personal cloud workspace, the only documentation is a six-page README from May, and the people who know the process leave by 31 December with no cover in place (S1, S2, S3).

stakeholder_confidence.rationale: Problematic because the scenario gives no direct evidence of executive or customer views. The risk committee's requirement for full documentation (S6) and the likely slip in sign-off make confidence fragile, so this is not treated as good news.

risks.description: Retraining knowledge is lost when the lead ML engineer leaves on 18 December, so the monthly retrain cannot be run reliably until a replacement is in post.
risks.mitigation: Before 18 December, record the retraining steps by running a supervised dry run with the lead engineer, and move the scripts and README into controlled company storage. Name a backup operator from the existing team and confirm they can run the next retrain without outside help.

risks.description: Full model documentation is not ready for the risk committee's 20 January validation sign-off, so the sign-off slips and the scale-up stalls.
risks.mitigation: Build a documentation gap list against the committee's requirements this week. Assign each gap to a named owner. Ask the committee secretary whether a conditional sign-off or a fixed later date is possible, and get the answer in writing before the 20 January date.

risks.description: Feature pipeline knowledge and access leave with the contractor on 31 December, so the pipeline cannot be maintained or debugged.
risks.mitigation: Hold a recorded handover session with the contractor before 31 December covering the feature pipeline design, failure modes and data sources. Transfer credentials and access to a company-controlled account, and confirm that the data platform team can run and repair the pipeline without the contractor.

risks.description: Triage accuracy keeps falling after the claim form change, pushing the model below the 85% target before sign-off.
risks.mitigation: Compare claim form fields before and after the change, and find which inputs now shift the model. Add a weekly accuracy check with a clear trigger, such as a drop below 86%, that pauses claim routing to the model and sends claims to standard handling.

risks.description: Credentials and access to the personal cloud workspace are lost or disputed after the leaver departs, blocking the retrain or the audit trail.
risks.mitigation: Remove dependence on the personal workspace now. Transfer ownership of the scripts and data to company accounts, rotate credentials, and log who holds access. Confirm the change with the risk committee as part of the documentation pack.

risks.description: The scale-up from 15% to all claims by end of March 2027 is delayed because the cost and timing are not yet planned.
risks.mitigation: Once sign-off is set, build a scale-up plan with cost, staffing and a stage gate for each volume step. Re-test the March 2027 date against that plan and report any change to the sponsor.

stabilize.goal: Stop the loss of retraining knowledge and access before the leavers depart, and stop the accuracy drop from getting worse.

actions.description: Move the retraining scripts, data pipeline code and README out of the personal cloud workspace into company-controlled storage, with the access list recorded.
actions.success_signal: All retraining scripts and the README are in company storage, and a named list of access holders exists.

actions.description: Run a recorded walkthrough of one full monthly retrain and feature pipeline run with the lead ML engineer and the contractor, and capture the steps in writing.
actions.success_signal: A signed walkthrough record exists, and a backup operator has followed it through to a completed dry run.

actions.description: Start a comparison of claim form fields before and after the change to find the cause of the accuracy drop.
actions.success_signal: A written finding names the form fields most linked to the accuracy drop, or states that the cause is still unknown.

actions.description: Get the risk committee's written position on the 20 January sign-off and the documentation it requires.
actions.success_signal: A written reply from the committee confirms the sign-off date or a fallback date.

recover.goal: Complete the model documentation the risk committee needs and confirm the sign-off date.

actions.description: Write the full model documentation against the committee's requirements, covering data sources, features, training, validation results and retraining steps.
actions.success_signal: A complete documentation pack has passed an internal review against the committee checklist.

actions.description: Secure interim consultant or contract cover, through a procurement exception if needed, to review the documentation and the retraining process.
actions.success_signal: A signed interim cover agreement is in place with a start date before the sign-off.

actions.description: Hold the documented handover of the feature pipeline and retraining process with the data platform team, and record gaps.
actions.success_signal: The data platform team has run the pipeline end to end, and any open gaps are logged with owners.

actions.description: Hold the committee pre-review and confirm whether the 20 January sign-off goes ahead.
actions.success_signal: The committee confirms in writing that the 20 January sign-off is kept or moved to a stated date.

sustain.goal: Keep the retraining process reliable after the replacement joins, and set up the scale-up under controls.

actions.description: Recruit the replacement ML engineer and plan a handover from the interim cover to the new hire.
actions.success_signal: A replacement offer is accepted with a confirmed start date, and a handover plan is agreed.

actions.description: Run the monthly retrain with the backup operator and report the accuracy result to the sponsor.
actions.success_signal: The retrain completes with a documented result, and accuracy is reported against the 85% target.

actions.description: Draft the scale-up plan from 15% to all claims with cost, staffing and stage gates.
actions.success_signal: A scale-up plan with stage gates and a cost estimate is presented to the sponsor for approval.

actions.description: Set up a standing weekly accuracy check and a rule for pausing model routing if accuracy falls below the agreed trigger.
actions.success_signal: The weekly check runs for four consecutive weeks, and the pause rule has been tested once.

stakeholder_updates.executive: The triage pilot is performing above its accuracy target, but the team faces a key-person risk: the two people who run monthly retraining leave by 31 December. The 20 January validation sign-off is at risk because the documentation is incomplete. Decisions needed: approve interim contract cover before 31 December, and confirm by early January whether the 20 January date holds or moves. The March 2027 scale-up date is not yet supported by a plan.
stakeholder_updates.delivery_team: The retraining scripts and pipeline are moving to company-controlled storage, and each person will be asked to take part in a recorded handover before 31 December. You will need to run the next retrain with support from the interim cover. Your priorities are the handover sessions, the documentation gap list and the weekly accuracy check. This is about closing a knowledge gap in the project, not about any individual's performance.
stakeholder_updates.customer: The claims triage pilot is working: accuracy is above target and handling time is down. We have identified a risk to the pace of rollout. Two members of the team are leaving, and we are making sure the model can be maintained and documented before it is expanded. We will confirm the timing of the next stage once the internal review has been completed.

decision_memo.context: The lead ML engineer leaves on 18 December and the contractor on 31 December, with no replacement before late February. The risk committee needs full documentation before its 20 January sign-off. The decision on how to protect the sign-off date and the retraining process is needed now, because the handover window closes at the end of December.

options.title: Hold the 20 January sign-off with interim consultant cover
options.trade_offs: Keeps the timeline and the March 2027 ambition if it works, but requires a procurement exception and a consultant to learn the scripts and write documentation in a few weeks. The risk is that the documentation is not ready and the sign-off fails.

options.title: Move the sign-off to a later date once the replacement is in post
options.trade_offs: Gives time for proper documentation and a full handover, and the replacement will be involved. The cost is a delay of at least two months, a likely slip in the scale-up, and a pilot that stays at 15% of claims for longer.

options.title: Pause the project and keep the model in its current pilot state
options.trade_offs: Stops new risk while the team stabilises the process. It does not solve the retraining knowledge gap or the accuracy drop, and it leaves the pilot exposed to a model that is not documented or maintained.

decision_memo.recommendation: Option 1, with a fallback. Secure interim cover now through a procurement exception, complete the handover before 31 December, and ask the committee to agree a fallback sign-off date in writing before 20 January. This keeps the pilot running at 15%, keeps the sign-off date in view, and avoids an unplanned stop. If the committee will not accept the documentation by 20 January, move to option 2 with the new date agreed.
success_metrics: A recorded handover covering the retraining process and pipeline is signed off before 31 December.
The next monthly retrain is completed by someone outside the two leavers, with documented results.
The risk committee confirms the sign-off date in writing by early January.
Triage accuracy stays at or above 85% for the pilot, with the cause of the drop from 89% to 87% documented.
A replacement ML engineer has an accepted offer and a confirmed start date before the end of January.
